# Aggappasāda Sutta (Iti 90 (It 3.41 PTS It 87))

**ID:** Iti 90 (It 3.41 PTS It 87)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Aggappasāda Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aggappasāda Sutta* ("The Best Kinds of Confidence", Iti 90) belongs to the third division (Tikanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* [Windisch 1889]. The discourse expounds three supreme objects of confidence (*tayo aggappasādā*): confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha [Windisch 1889]. The prose proclaims the Buddha as the foremost (*agga*) among all beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed, with form or formless, percipient or non-percipient; the Dhamma of detachment (*virāga*) as foremost among all phenomena; and the Saṅgha of eight noble persons (*aṭṭha purisapuggalā*) as the unexcelled field of merit for the world [Windisch 1889]. It explains that for those who place confidence in the foremost, the resulting fruit is also foremost (*agge pasannānaṁ aggo vipāko hoti*), concluding with verses beginning *Aggato ve pasannānaṁ* [Windisch 1889].

 Passage-level and resembling parallels include AN 5.32 (*Cundīsutta*), SN 45.139, and SĀ 902–904, and the text is also cited in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) and *Milindapañha*. DharmaNexus confirms these connections with extensive text reuse across 32 Pali texts, sharing the vast majority of the discourse (§2.1–8.4) with AN 4.34, alongside substantial passages with AN 5.32, SN 45.139, and Ne 37 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus identify shared material with Chinese Āgamas (T 125 and T 99), Tibetan translations in the Kangyur (*Pūrṇapramukha-avadānaśataka*) and Tengyur, and the Sanskrit *Ratnamālāvadāna* [DharmaNexus]. In broader Buddhist literature, Étienne Lamotte notes that this doctrinal topic is designated *aggappasāda* in Pali and *agraprajñapti* in Sanskrit sources such as the *Mahāvastu*, *Divyāvadāna*, and *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [Lamotte, Traité].
